steps.title: Obtain Ethics and Trial Registration
steps.instruction: Secure ethics approval from the University of Cambridge Psychology Research Ethics Committee (ref PRE.2015.108) and Universitas Gadjah Mada (ref 1237/SD/PL.03.07/IV/2016); obtain trial insurance (Cambridge ref 609/M/C/1510); obtain permission from the Yogyakarta Provincial Government (ref 070/REG/V/625/5/2016); register the trial on clinicaltrials.gov (NCT02700490) on 25 Feb 2016.

steps.title: Recruit and Train Research Assistants
steps.instruction: Advertise recruitment flyers at Universitas Gadjah Mada and on social media; interview 30 % of applicants and hire 28 assistants (≈10 % of applicants) for the substantive study; select candidates with high education, people‑skills and arithmetic ability (medical graduates or social‑science masters). Train all assistants on the GHQ‑12, WHODAS 2.0, EQ‑5D‑3L, CSRI, consent procedures, and the screening flowchart (hard‑copy and digital). Inform them of random audits. Pay a base salary of Rp 100 000 (~£6) per day; add a transport allowance equal to one day’s salary for assistants stationed >3 h drive from Yogyakarta centre. Assign two assistants per Puskesmas (a junior doctor plus a medical student or registered nurse).

steps.title: Prepare Site Logistics and Cluster Assignment
steps.instruction: Send letters of approval and an information pack to all 28 selected Puskesmas; hold a one‑day briefing with heads of Puskesmas, all clinicians, and district health representatives; assign each Puskesmas a unique cluster number; ensure each Puskesmas has ISO certification so data collection can be embedded in routine patient flow.

steps.title: Conduct Participant Screening
steps.instruction: During the substantive recruitment period (two weeks), research assistants check in each morning at 07:00 h, take a self‑portrait with a designated object (e.g., queue‑number counter) and send a picture of the empty clinic at checkout. Provide every adult primary‑care attendee (≈40 patients/day) with the GHQ‑12 and a demographic questionnaire (CSRI) at the registration counter when they receive a queue number; ask them to self‑complete while waiting for blood‑pressure measurement. Score GHQ‑12 using the bimodal 0‑0‑1‑1 method; identify participants with a score ≥ 2 (threshold for inclusion). Record the number of screenings completed each day and compare with Puskesmas attendance to calculate the percentage screened. In the pilot (June 2016) one‑week screening yielded 5 341 patients screened.

steps.title: Obtain Informed Consent
steps.instruction: Approach eligible patients, explain trial objectives, and reassure that participation is voluntary and will not affect usual care. Provide an information sheet and answer questions. For literate participants, obtain written signature; for illiterate participants, obtain thumb‑print and a witness signature. Double‑check understanding of follow‑up requirements and right to withdraw.

steps.title: Administer Baseline Questionnaires
steps.instruction: Give consented participants a questionnaire booklet containing the self‑administered WHODAS 2.0 (36‑item) and EQ‑5D‑3L. Allow illiterate participants to be interviewed by a research assistant who completes the booklet on their behalf. Collect completed booklets before the participant meets the assigned clinician.

steps.title: Deliver Intervention – WHO mhGAP Arm
steps.instruction: Pass the participant’s medical record and questionnaire booklet to the Puskesmas doctor trained in the Indonesian‑adapted WHO mhGAP framework. Doctor conducts a standard medical consultation, then completes the structured interview (CIS‑R and HoNOS) located in the second half of the booklet. Record participant name, medical‑record number, and contact details separately. Develop a treatment plan (pharmacological therapy, psychosocial intervention, or referral) together with the participant and ask the participant to return for further therapy sessions as needed.

steps.title: Deliver Intervention – Specialist Co‑location Arm
steps.instruction: Pass the participant’s medical record and questionnaire booklet to a general practitioner for routine physical care, then refer the participant to the on‑site clinical psychologist. Psychologist conducts the structured interview (CIS‑R and HoNOS) in the second half of the booklet, records name, medical‑record number, and contact details separately, and decides on psychotherapy, medication, or other interventions. Ask the participant to return for further therapy sessions if indicated.

steps.title: Record Clinician Diagnosis
steps.instruction: At the end of the CIS‑R/HoNOS interview, the clinician records a diagnostic label in the booklet based on clinical judgment (not on CIS‑R score). This diagnosis determines whether the participant is scheduled for follow‑up therapy.

steps.title: Perform Six‑Month Follow‑up Assessment
steps.instruction: Six months after baseline, blinded research assistants contact participants by telephone 1–2 weeks before a home visit. Ensure safety: park the moped outside the participant’s home, keep personal belongings with the researcher, carry a fully‑charged mobile phone, and be accompanied by a Puskesmas representative. Conduct the follow‑up interview alone with the participant (room unlocked). Re‑administer WHODAS 2.0 (self‑report), EQ‑5D‑3L (self‑report), CIS‑R, and HoNOS. Do not assign a new diagnosis.

steps.title: Manage Participant Confidentiality and Data
steps.instruction: Keep all personal contact details (phone numbers, addresses) confidential and stored separately from outcome data. Ensure field researchers do not share participant identifiers with other team members.

steps.title: Calculate Service Use Costs
steps.instruction: Apply nationally applicable unit costs (2017 Rupiah) to each reported service use: outpatient primary‑care Rp 13 961, inpatient Rp 93 052 (≈£1 ≈ Rp 19 000 in Mar 2018). Adjust 2012 unit costs for inflation using Statista Indonesia inflation rates. Estimate psychologist consultation cost: monthly salary Rp 3 000 000 (Jan 2017) ÷ 231 monthly appointments = Rp 12 987; add infrastructure/retribution Rp 2 100 for a total of Rp 15 087 per appointment. For the Specialist arm baseline cost, combine GP consultation (including retribution) with psychologist consultation (without retribution) to total Rp 30 468.

steps.title: Determine Sample Size and Power
steps.instruction: Assume α = 0.05, power = 0.80, SD = 5.2, non‑inferiority margin δ₀ = 2 for HoNOS. Individual‑randomised sample size = 84. Inflate for clustering using ICC = 0.1: required per‑arm sample ≈ 189. Anticipate 20 % attrition; target ≈ 227 participants per arm (≈ 16 per Puskesmas). Re‑calculate ICC after baseline recruitment using Jiang’s one‑way ANOVA formula.

steps.title: Analyze Primary and Secondary Outcomes
steps.instruction: Use STATA 13. Clean outcome and baseline data blinded to allocation. Summarise data, compare characteristics of completers vs non‑completers. Fit mixed‑effects random‑effects regression models with random intercept for Puskesmas (level 2) and fixed effects for treatment allocation and baseline score. Apply intention‑to‑treat principle. For missing follow‑up data, perform multiple imputation by chained equations (MICE) with predictive‑mean‑matching.

steps.title: Conduct Economic Evaluation
steps.instruction: Calculate incremental cost‑effectiveness ratios (ICERs) for HoNOS and QALYs (derived from EQ‑5D‑3L using Thai and Malaysian value sets; Malaysian set preferred for Indonesia). Estimate QALYs via area‑under‑the‑curve over 6 months. Bootstrap 1 000 resamples to obtain uncertainty distributions; plot cost‑effectiveness plane and generate cost‑effectiveness acceptability curves. Compare ICERs against Indonesian willingness‑to‑pay thresholds (e.g., three times GDP per capita or locally derived thresholds).
